office.remit: Council-manager city (Charter Section 1-2). The five-member council (one at-large member and one from each of four wards; the council elects the mayor and vice mayor from its members, Charter Section 2-2) sets policy, adopts the budget and ordinances, awards public improvement contracts and approves purchases above the ordinance threshold. The city manager is the chief administrative officer: appoints and supervises all department heads, prepares and administers the budget, makes purchases below the council threshold and signs permits and state filings as the city's responsible official (Charter Sections 3-3, 4-2, 4-4). Council members are unpaid (Section 2-3) and deal with staff only through the manager (Section 2-5). The council also sits as the trustees of the Ada Public Works Authority (APWA), the public trust that operates water, wastewater, sanitation and the landfill; APWA meets right after each council meeting. Council meets the first and third Mondays at 5:45 p.m. in the council chamber at City Hall. Fiscal year July 1-June 30 (Section 4-5). Constituent mail to the city manager's office comes through the contact form on adaok.com and citymanager@adaok.com; the office replies in the manager's name.

succession.rule: Charter of the City of Ada, Section 3-1: 'There shall be a city manager. The council shall appoint him for an indefinite term by a vote of a majority of all its members. It shall choose him solely on the basis of his executive and administrative qualifications. At the time of his appointment, he need not be a resident of the city or state; but, during his tenure of office, he shall reside within the city.' Section 2-4(1): the council has power 'To appoint and remove the city manager'. Section 3-2: the council may appoint an acting city manager when the manager has not designated one. State law is to the same effect for statutory council-manager cities (11 O.S. 10-112).
succession.timeline: Tue Sept 1: special council meeting accepts the previous city manager's resignation, effective that day, and appoints Assistant City Manager Renee Calloway acting city manager. Mon Sept 14 and Wed Sept 16: council interviews three candidates in executive session. Mon Sept 21: council appoints Neil Hartsock city manager, 4-1, and approves his employment agreement. Wed Sept 23: Hartsock starts.
